paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus goes to the people everybody else walks past. He sees Matthew at the tax booth and says, "Follow Me," and Matthew gets up and follows Him (Matthew 9:9). Then He sits down to eat with tax collectors and sinners, and the Pharisees want to know why (Matthew 9:10-11). Jesus doesn't argue. He says, "It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick" (Matthew 9:12).

So hear this, baker: you don't have to clean yourself up before you come to Jesus. He says, "I desire mercy, not sacrifice," and "I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners" (Matthew 9:13). I spent years in a junk drawer thinking I had to be shiny first, and I was WRONG. The Doctor is already in the room, so you don't have to hide the sick part. And once you've been called, you can show that same mercy to the next person who shows up at your table.

The fasting question and the patch and the wineskins all say one thing: Jesus is doing something new, and it can't be squeezed into the old way of doing things. Jesus calls Himself the bridegroom, and while He is with them, His disciples are like wedding guests who can't mourn (Matthew 9:15). He says, "Neither do men pour new wine into old wineskins," because the skins would burst, but new wine goes into new wineskins, "and both are preserved" (Matthew 9:17). So let Him make you new, friend, and then stay ready for the celebration.
